title: Runtime record primitives
description: Shared shapes for Kiln's five persisted runtime records. ⚠️ SEPARATE FROM THE ARTIFACT `common.schema.json` ON PURPOSE. These records are not artifacts: they carry no ID prefix, no review status, no lifecycle, no trace links, and they version on their OWN cadence — an artifact `schemaVersion` tracks the CONTENT model (#50) and says nothing about the shape of a consent record. Sharing one envelope would tie two release cycles together for the sake of a field name they happen to spell alike. ⚠️ WHAT IS SHARED WITH THE ARTIFACT LAYER IS THE MACHINERY, NOT THE VOCABULARY: the same Ajv 2020-12 construction, the same dialect check, the same error formatter and the same ValidationError. A second schema implementation is what this avoids; a second vocabulary is what it deliberately keeps.

recordVersion.description: The shape version of THIS record. ⚠️ Per record, not per project: these five files are written by different phases, migrate independently, and a single number would force a migration on four of them because the fifth changed.

isoTimestamp.description: An instant, where the instant is part of what the record MEANS — a consent grant, a transaction start. ⚠️ Not to be added out of habit: a timestamp recording when a committed file was written duplicates what version control already knows, and a timestamp inside a cache key is operational noise that invalidates the cache every run.

projectId.description: The generated, stable, non-secret project identifier. ⚠️ LOWERCASE HEX AND FIXED LENGTH BECAUSE IT BECOMES A DIRECTORY NAME: external user-local state lives under `<state-root>/projects/<projectId>/`, so anything needing escaping, case-folding or length negotiation would be a portability bug waiting on the first Windows/POSIX pair. ⚠️ It carries no meaning and derives from nothing — not from the project name, not from a path. A derived id would leak whatever it derived from into an ignored directory name and change when that thing was renamed.

relativePath.description: A path relative to the project root, with `/` separators. ⚠️ ABSOLUTE PATHS ARE REJECTED BY THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN BY A REVIEWER, because REQ-0024 forbids an absolute user-home path in anything Kiln writes and these records are the files most likely to accumulate one. Drive letters, UNC prefixes, leading slashes and any `..` segment are all refused. ⚠️ This is validation and not containment — only resolution against the canonicalised root is a boundary (#86), and that lives in `lib/content-root.mjs`.

digest.description: A content digest, algorithm-prefixed so a later change of algorithm is visible in the data rather than inferred from length. ⚠️ NEVER OVER CREDENTIAL MATERIAL. Section 3.12 forbids storing a credential-derived fingerprint, and a digest is exactly that: hashing a key does not make it safe to persist, it makes it an oracle for confirming a guess.
